beats.text: It was all demoed at once.
beats.note: The mouse, windows, hypertext, video calls, live shared editing — shown working together in San Francisco in 1968, before any of it was a product.

beats.name: Douglas Engelbart
beats.role: 9 December, a 90-minute session at the Fall Joint Computer Conference. He sat alone on stage under the lights, driving a computer the audience could not see.

beats.context: The computer was in Menlo Park, that far away. A homemade 2,400-baud modem carried his keystrokes; microwave dishes beamed the video back.

beats.lead: The pointer already had its name
beats.text: The cord looked like a tail.
beats.note: Bill English built the first mouse in 1964 from Engelbart's sketches: a wooden shell, two metal wheels, one button. On stage, Engelbart admitted nobody remembered who named it.

beats.text: He remembered the crowd standing, cheering like crazy.

beats.line: Steven Levy later gave it a title: the mother of all demos.
